# T2.09: frame sizes

`encode1 W H 26` with the T2.05e settings (`NVENC_VAR=sliceauto,ssd,bh=2,tileada`), one IDR frame, decoded by
Apple's software decoder (`h264check`):

| size | encode (doorbell → semaphore) | bits | luma PSNR | chroma PSNR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 256x128 | 0.09 ms | 9 064 | 45.25 dB | 45.82 dB |
| 1280x720 | 0.93 ms | 216 672 | 45.77 dB | 46.85 dB |
| 1920x1080 | 2.02 ms | 485 808 | 45.84 dB | 46.76 dB |
| 3840x2160 | 7.87 ms | 1 920 424 | 45.84 dB | 46.90 dB |
| 3840x2025 | 7.39 ms | 1 834 664 | 45.78 dB | 46.84 dB |

Fixes needed on the way:
- **Recon buffer overrun.** 1280x720 and 3840x2160 first hit `FAULT_PTE` right past the end of the reconstructed
  picture buffer: the engine writes the planes with rows rounded up (720 → at least 736). The recon planes are now
  32-row rounded, plus 64 KB of slack. Sizes whose MB rows are a multiple of 2 (256x128, 1920x1088) hid this.
- **Odd heights.** `encode1` and `h264check` used `H/2` chroma rows; now `(H+1)/2`. H.264 4:2:0 crops in 2-pixel
  units, so a 2025-row picture is signalled as 2026 rows (the decoder reports 3840x2026; PSNR is measured on the 2025
  real rows). Unlike nullmoth's library, the engine itself has no problem with odd heights.

Notes for later:
- 4K takes ~7.9 ms per IDR at these settings (intra 4x4 + 16x16, SSD on all three sizes). Mode-decision settings
  (the reference uses 16x16 intra only, ip_search 7, rdo 1) and P-frames will change that. Measure again in M3/M5.
- The input layout (`nvenc_in_tile_plane`, 64x16 tiles) holds for pitches 256 to 3840: no pitch-dependent effect.
